messages.text: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes

metadata.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
metadata.content: Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle delves into the talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix, assessing F1's newest venue and where it can be improved, the debate around the rules that cost Lando Norris, and Kimi Antonelli's ever-growing world championship lead Martin Brundle Expert Analyst @MBrundleF1 Monday 14 September 2026 16:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See how Lando Norris lost the lead and a likely win at the Spanish Grand Prix after an untimely Virtual Safety Car for the McLaren driver The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers. It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges. The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least. messages.text: Are the Giants back? 'They can be playoff team!'

metadata.summary: The New York Giants opened the John Harbaugh era with a statement win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday and Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold has backed their first-year head coach to steer them back into playoff contention.
metadata.content: New York Giants can make NFL playoffs with new John Harbaugh culture, says Jeff Reinebold | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis New York Giants can make NFL playoffs with new John Harbaugh culture, says Jeff Reinebold The New York Giants began their season with a divisional win over the Dallas Cowboys as they seek a return to the playoffs; listen to Inside the Huddle podcast throughout the season as Neil Reynolds, Phoebe Schecter and Jeff Reinebold discuss the biggest storylines Monday 14 September 2026 14:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the opening weekend NFL match between the New York Giants and the Dallas Cowboys The New York Giants opened the John Harbaugh era with a statement win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday and Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold has backed their first-year head coach to steer them back into playoff contention. Harbaugh took the reins on a coasting Giants organisation earlier this year after parting from the Baltimore Ravens following 18 seasons as head coach. Awaiting him was a team of young talent seeking direction after just two winning seasons in the last 10 years, with Jaxson Dart inspiring fresh hope at quarterback alongside a pass rush tipped to join the league's elite units.
